name: Bahrain
main_industries: Finance · Fintech · Manufacturing · Tourism · Logistics
summary: Most open GCC economy with strong fintech and financial services
key_industry_1_desc: Bahrain is the GCCs most open financial market. CBB regulates a mature ecosystem of banks, insurers and fintechs.
key_industry_2_desc: Bahrain is a regional cloud hub hosting AWS, Microsoft Azure and Google Cloud MEA infrastructure.
key_industry_3_desc: ALBA is one of the worlds largest aluminium smelters. Manufacturing sector contributes 14% of GDP.
key_industry_4_desc: Bahrain Tourism and Exhibitions Authority targeting 14M visitors annually. Strong weekend tourism from Saudi Arabia.
talent_overview: Bahrain has the most liberal labour market in the GCC. Workers can change jobs without employer permission under flexi-permit system.
talent_localisation_rule: Bahrainisation targets range from 5% in oil sector to 50% in retail. Financial sector has specific CBB requirements.
talent_foreign_worker_rule: Work permit via Labour Market Regulatory Authority. Flexi-permit available for self-sponsored workers.
talent_key_consideration: Bahrain offers the most flexible labour mobility in the GCC making it attractive for firms needing workforce agility.
sector_priority_1_why: CBB regulatory sandbox and 0% tax environment make Bahrain the most accessible GCC market for fintech firms.
sector_priority_2_why: Bahrain Cloud First policy and major hyperscaler presence creating strong demand for cloud services and solutions.
sector_priority_3_why: Khalifa Bin Salman Port expansion and proximity to Saudi Arabia creating strong logistics and distribution opportunities.
entry_playbook_overview: Bahrain is the fastest and most straightforward GCC market to enter. 100% foreign ownership permitted across most sectors.
entry_step_1: Register via Sijilaat — Bahrains one-stop online business registration portal. Process takes 1 to 3 days
entry_step_2: Obtain sector specific licences — CBB licence for financial services, other regulators for relevant sectors
entry_step_3: Open corporate bank account — Bahrain has a mature banking sector with straightforward KYC processes
entry_step_4: Register with National Bureau for Revenue — VAT registration required if turnover exceeds BHD 37,500
geopolitical_alert: Hit in earlier strike waves and hosts major foreign naval infrastructure; Hormuz-dependent trade disrupted.
current_conditions_summary: The Strait of Hormuz has been effectively closed to commercial shipping since 28 Feb 2026 (single-digit daily transits vs ~85 pre-crisis); the US naval blockade of Iran was reinstated in mid-July after the interim ceasefire collapsed. US–Iran talks are under way — on 23 Sep Iran tabled a road map including a 60-day regionwide ceasefire and phased reopening, not yet agreed. Bahrain hosts major foreign naval infrastructure, raising its exposure.
current_conditions_factors: Prior strikes · Naval-hub exposure · Hormuz closure
current_conditions_outlook: Financial-services base remains, but conditions are severely impaired near term.

name: Bangladesh
main_industries: Garments · Remittances · Agriculture · Pharma · IT Services
summary: Rising garment powerhouse with growing middle class
key_industry_1_desc: Bangladesh is worlds 2nd largest garment exporter after China with $47B in annual exports to EU and US.
key_industry_2_desc: Bangladesh pharma sector meets 98% of domestic demand and exports to 150+ countries. LDC status provides IP flexibility.
key_industry_3_desc: Bangladesh exports $1B+ in IT services. Government Digital Bangladesh initiative driving tech sector development.
key_industry_4_desc: Agriculture employs 40% of workforce. Rice, jute and fish are top commodities with growing agritech investment.
talent_overview: Bangladesh has a young workforce of 70M with improving education levels. Competitive labour costs. English used in business and export sectors.
talent_localisation_rule: Foreign nationals cannot exceed 5% of total workforce in most sectors. BIDA approval required for expatriate hiring above threshold.
talent_foreign_worker_rule: Work permit from BIDA required. Linked to specific employer. Process takes 6 to 10 weeks.
talent_key_consideration: Bangladesh offers Asias most competitive garment manufacturing labour costs alongside a growing pool of technology talent.
sector_priority_1_why: Bangladesh RMG sector upgrading to higher value technical textiles and knitwear creating investment opportunity in manufacturing technology.
sector_priority_2_why: Government Hi-Tech Parks and competitive English speaking talent creating growing IT services and BPO investment opportunity.
sector_priority_3_why: LDC IP flexibilities until 2033 and low cost manufacturing creating opportunity for generic pharmaceutical production investment.
entry_playbook_overview: Bangladesh market entry is managed through BIDA. Special Economic Zones offer streamlined entry for export oriented manufacturing.
entry_step_1: Register with BIDA — Bangladesh Investment Development Authority is the one stop service for foreign investors
entry_step_2: Consider SEZ location — BEZA economic zones offer duty benefits and streamlined licencing for manufacturing investment
entry_step_3: Register with NBR — National Board of Revenue for tax identification and VAT registration
entry_step_4: Open bank account with authorised dealer — required for foreign exchange management and remittance approvals
geopolitical_alert: Energy disruption from the Hormuz closure (LNG and fuel imports) is straining power supply and industrial output.
current_conditions_summary: Bangladesh depends on imported LNG and fuel from the Gulf; the Hormuz closure has disrupted power supply and industrial output.
current_conditions_factors: LNG/fuel disruption · Power supply strain · Export-sector risk
current_conditions_outlook: Plan for energy-supply contingencies; manufacturing timelines at risk.

alerts.title: Investment Board Restructured
alerts.summary: Bangladesh Investment Development Authority restructured to streamline foreign investment approvals.

alerts.title: New Investment Authority
alerts.summary: Bangladesh Investment Development Authority restructured as Bangladesh Investment Authority with enhanced powers to approve and facilitate foreign investments.

name: China
main_industries: Manufacturing · Technology · Finance · Retail · Infrastructure
summary: Worlds second largest economy — complex but unmissable
key_industry_1_desc: China is the worlds factory producing 28% of global manufacturing output. Upgrading rapidly to high tech and advanced manufacturing.
key_industry_2_desc: China dominates global EV production with 60% market share. BYD, NIO and CATL are global leaders.
key_industry_3_desc: Alibaba, JD.com and Pinduoduo drive $2T+ in annual e-commerce. Digital payments via Alipay and WeChat Pay are universal.
key_industry_4_desc: Shanghai is a major global financial centre. PBOC is internationalising RMB. Bond and equity markets are the worlds 2nd largest.
talent_overview: China has the worlds largest graduate pool with 10M+ annual graduates. Mandarin is essential for most roles. English limited outside major cities.
talent_localisation_rule: No formal minimum localisation quota but practical and cultural expectations strongly favour local hiring at all levels.
talent_foreign_worker_rule: Work permit Z visa required. Employer sponsored. Foreign talent points based system applies. Process takes 4 to 8 weeks.
talent_key_consideration: Local Chinese management is strongly preferred by government and customers. Investing in Chinese leadership pipeline is essential.
sector_priority_1_why: China green technology dominance creating partnership opportunities for foreign firms in EV battery, solar and wind supply chains.
sector_priority_2_why: Ageing population and government healthcare investment creating significant medical device, pharma and hospital management opportunities.
sector_priority_3_why: Made in China 2025 creating partnership and technology licensing opportunities in robotics, semiconductors and aerospace.
entry_playbook_overview: China market entry requires careful structure selection and regulatory navigation. WFOE is most common for operational control.
entry_step_1: Select entry structure — WFOE for full operational control, JV for restricted sectors, RO for initial market research
entry_step_2: Register with SAMR — State Administration for Market Regulation for business licence in chosen city
entry_step_3: Register with SAT — State Administration of Taxation for corporate tax, VAT and withholding tax registration
entry_step_4: Complete data and cybersecurity compliance — PIPL, DSL and Cybersecurity Law requirements must be addressed before launch
current_conditions_summary: No direct exposure to the Iran conflict. Higher global oil prices (Brent above US$100 in late Sep 2026) and shipping disruption raise operating and logistics costs.
current_conditions_factors: Normal business environment · Standard regulatory monitoring · No elevated conflict exposure
current_conditions_outlook: Current conditions broadly consistent with structural fundamentals. Standard market entry timing considerations apply.

alerts.title: Data Export Rules Clarified
alerts.summary: CAC issued updated guidance on cross-border data transfer security assessments.

name: Egypt
main_industries: Tourism · Oil & Gas · Remittances · Manufacturing · Agriculture
summary: Largest Arab economy with 100M+ consumer market
key_industry_1_desc: Egypt is a significant natural gas producer. Zohr field is Mediterraneans largest. Renewable energy pipeline is growing.
key_industry_2_desc: Egypt targets 30M visitors by 2028. Antiquities, Red Sea resorts and new mega-projects are driving investment.
key_industry_3_desc: Egypt is building an industrial manufacturing base in automotive, textiles and food processing targeting African exports.
key_industry_4_desc: Egypt has 100M+ population with low banking penetration creating significant fintech and digital finance opportunity.
talent_overview: Egypt has one of Africas largest talent pools with 700,000+ university graduates annually. Arabic is primary business language.
talent_localisation_rule: Egyptian Labour Law requires minimum 90% Egyptian nationals in company workforce. Exceptions apply for specialist roles.
talent_foreign_worker_rule: Work permit required from Ministry of Manpower. Quota based on company size. Process takes 4 to 8 weeks.
talent_key_consideration: Egypt offers highly cost competitive professional talent, particularly in engineering, IT and finance.
sector_priority_1_why: Egypt targets 42% renewable energy by 2030. Benban solar park and wind projects creating significant investment pipeline.
sector_priority_2_why: New administrative capital and Red Sea resort developments creating significant hotel and hospitality investment demand.
sector_priority_3_why: Central Bank of Egypt fintech sandbox and 60M+ unbanked population creating significant digital finance opportunity.
entry_playbook_overview: Egypt offers multiple entry structures. General Authority for Investment is the primary entry point for foreign investors.
entry_step_1: Register with GAFI — General Authority for Investment and Free Zones is the one stop shop for foreign investors
entry_step_2: Choose your structure — LLC is most common. Free zone options available for export oriented businesses
entry_step_3: Register with Egyptian Tax Authority — corporate tax at 22.5% applies. VAT registration required above threshold
entry_step_4: Open EGP and USD bank accounts — dual currency accounts essential given FX management requirements
geopolitical_alert: Suez Canal traffic recovered strongly as Hormuz trade reroutes (Aug 2026 revenue US$567m vs US$326m a year earlier), but the Houthis seized the Bab al-Mandeb coastline on 13 Sep 2026, renewing Red Sea shipping risk.
current_conditions_summary: Suez Canal revenues rebounded in August 2026 (US$567m vs US$326m a year earlier) as trade reroutes away from Hormuz. On 13 Sep 2026 the Houthis took control of Yemen's Red Sea coastline including Perim Island, effectively controlling the Bab al-Mandeb strait — a renewed risk to Red Sea and Suez traffic. EGP around 51 per USD.
current_conditions_factors: Suez rebound · Bab al-Mandeb risk · FX pressure
current_conditions_outlook: Watch Red Sea shipping over the next quarter; canal revenue gains could reverse quickly.

alerts.title: IMF Programme Review Passed
alerts.summary: Egypt successfully completed fourth IMF programme review unlocking next tranche of funding. FX stability improving with interbank rate stabilising around EGP 48-50 per USD.

name: Ethiopia
main_industries: Agriculture · Manufacturing · Construction · Tourism · Telecoms
summary: Africas second most populous nation with high growth potential
key_industry_1_desc: Ethiopia is the birthplace of coffee and Africas largest coffee exporter. Agriculture employs 70% of the population.
key_industry_2_desc: Government industrial parks hosting H&M, PVH and Decathlon garment suppliers offer subsidised utilities and land.
key_industry_3_desc: Safaricom Ethiopia launched 2022. Telebirr mobile money growing rapidly in a market with low financial inclusion.
key_industry_4_desc: Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam makes Ethiopia Africas largest power producer. Significant power export potential to neighbours.
talent_overview: Ethiopia has a young population of 126M with improving education. Amharic is official language. English used in business and government.
talent_localisation_rule: Ethiopian Investment Law requires employment of Ethiopian nationals except for senior management and technical specialist roles.
talent_foreign_worker_rule: Work permit from Ministry of Labour required. Investment permit holders get facilitated work permit processing.
talent_key_consideration: Ethiopia offers Africas lowest labour costs making it compelling for labour intensive manufacturing despite infrastructure limitations.
sector_priority_1_why: Government industrial parks offer lowest African manufacturing costs with duty free export access to US and EU markets.
sector_priority_2_why: Vast arable land, growing domestic market and export potential making food processing one of Africas best investment opportunities.
sector_priority_3_why: GERD hydropower surplus and strong solar potential creating power export and green manufacturing investment opportunities.
entry_playbook_overview: Ethiopia investment entry managed through Ethiopian Investment Commission. Industrial park entry offers the most streamlined route for manufacturers.
entry_step_1: Register with EIC — Ethiopian Investment Commission is the one stop shop for foreign investment registration and facilitation
entry_step_2: Obtain investment permit — EIC issues investment permit specifying approved business activities and minimum capital
entry_step_3: Register with commercial court — business registration with Federal First Instance Court following investment permit
entry_step_4: Register with ERCA — Ethiopian Revenue and Customs Authority for tax identification and VAT registration
current_conditions_summary: No direct exposure to the Iran conflict. Higher global oil prices (Brent above US$100 in late Sep 2026) and shipping disruption raise operating and logistics costs.
current_conditions_factors: Normal business environment · Standard regulatory monitoring · No elevated conflict exposure
current_conditions_outlook: Current conditions broadly consistent with structural fundamentals. Standard market entry timing considerations apply.

name: India
main_industries: IT Services · Pharma · Manufacturing · Agriculture · Finance
summary: Worlds fastest growing major economy with massive opportunity
key_industry_1_desc: India IT sector exports $245B annually. Bengaluru, Hyderabad and Pune are global technology delivery hubs.
key_industry_2_desc: Production Linked Incentive schemes covering 14 sectors are attracting global manufacturers to India.
key_industry_3_desc: UPI processes 10B+ transactions monthly. India is the worlds 3rd largest fintech ecosystem by deal volume.
key_industry_4_desc: India targets 500GW renewable capacity by 2030. Solar and green hydrogen are priority investment sectors.
talent_overview: India produces 1.5M engineering graduates annually. English is the business language. Deep talent pools in IT, finance, pharma and engineering.
talent_localisation_rule: No mandatory localisation requirement for most sectors. State level employment requirements vary. Priority to local hiring is culturally expected.
talent_foreign_worker_rule: Business Visa or Employment Visa required. Employment Visa requires minimum salary of $25,000 per annum.
talent_key_consideration: India offers the worlds largest English speaking technical talent pool at highly competitive cost making it ideal for global capability centres.
sector_priority_1_why: India hosts 1,600+ GCCs for global firms. Cost, talent scale and English proficiency make it unrivalled for technology delivery.
sector_priority_2_why: India solar and green hydrogen targets creating the worlds largest renewable energy investment pipeline outside China.
sector_priority_3_why: PLI incentives in electronics, pharma, textiles and 11 other sectors creating compelling manufacturing investment opportunities.
entry_playbook_overview: India offers multiple entry structures. Wholly owned subsidiary is most common for foreign firms. State selection matters enormously.
entry_step_1: Incorporate with MCA — Ministry of Corporate Affairs SPICe+ portal for company registration. Process takes 3 to 7 days
entry_step_2: Obtain PAN and TAN — Permanent Account Number and Tax Deduction Account Number from Income Tax Department
entry_step_3: Register for GST — Goods and Services Tax registration required if turnover exceeds INR 2 million
entry_step_4: Select your state — Karnataka, Maharashtra, Telangana and Tamil Nadu offer best infrastructure and talent for technology firms
geopolitical_alert: Oil-import shock from the Hormuz closure: Brent above US$100 and the rupee at record lows (~96 per USD, Sep 2026). USD-denominated labour costs are lower; input and energy costs higher.
current_conditions_summary: India imports most of its crude, much of it historically via Hormuz. With Brent above US$100 and the rupee at record lows (~96 per USD in Sep 2026), import costs and inflation pressures are elevated. For foreign firms, USD-denominated labour costs have fallen.
current_conditions_factors: Oil-import shock · Record-low rupee · Lower USD labour costs
current_conditions_outlook: Long-term thesis intact; hedge FX and budget for higher energy and logistics costs.

alerts.summary: Digital Personal Data Protection Rules formally notified. Companies must appoint Data Protection Officers and implement consent mechanisms by June 2026.

name: Indonesia
main_industries: Commodities · Manufacturing · Digital Economy · Agriculture · Finance
summary: Southeast Asias largest economy with 270M consumer market
key_industry_1_desc: Indonesia has the worlds 4th largest internet population. Tokopedia, Gojek and Traveloka are Southeast Asias largest tech firms.
key_industry_2_desc: Indonesia is the worlds largest nickel producer and top coal exporter. EV battery supply chain investment is surging.
key_industry_3_desc: Indonesia is becoming a China plus one manufacturing destination for textiles, electronics and automotive components.
key_industry_4_desc: Indonesia has 180M+ unbanked adults. GoPay, OVO and Dana are driving rapid digital payment adoption.
talent_overview: Indonesia has a young workforce of 140M with improving university output. Bahasa Indonesia is the business language with English in multinationals.
talent_localisation_rule: Manpower Law requires a ratio of Indonesian to foreign workers. Sponsor must develop a workforce development plan for each expatriate.
talent_foreign_worker_rule: RPTKA work plan approval required before hiring expatriates. KITAS stay permit required. Process takes 4 to 8 weeks.
talent_key_consideration: Jakarta has a competitive senior talent market. Surabaya and other cities offer cost effective alternatives for back office functions.
sector_priority_1_why: Indonesia controls 40% of global nickel reserves and is positioning as the centre of the global EV battery supply chain.
sector_priority_2_why: 210M internet users and growing middle class making Indonesia SEAs most compelling digital economy investment destination.
sector_priority_3_why: Indonesia targeting 23% renewable energy by 2025 with geothermal, solar and hydro creating significant investment pipeline.
entry_playbook_overview: Indonesia requires a PT PMA foreign investment company. BKPM is the investment coordination board managing foreign investment approvals.
entry_step_1: Establish PT PMA via OSS — Online Single Submission system is the single window for business licencing and investment approvals
entry_step_2: Check negative investment list — confirms which sectors are open to foreign investment and applicable ownership limits
entry_step_3: Meet minimum investment requirement — IDR 10 billion minimum investment applies to most PT PMA companies
entry_step_4: Register with DJP — Directorate General of Taxation for NPWP tax identification number and PKP VAT registration
current_conditions_summary: No direct exposure to the Iran conflict. Higher global oil prices (Brent above US$100 in late Sep 2026) and shipping disruption raise operating and logistics costs.

name: Kazakhstan
main_industries: Oil & Gas · Mining · Agriculture · Finance · Manufacturing
summary: Central Asian powerhouse with significant natural resources
key_industry_1_desc: Kazakhstan is the worlds 12th largest oil producer. Tengiz, Kashagan and Karachaganak fields attract major international operators.
key_industry_2_desc: Kazakhstan holds top 10 global reserves of uranium, chromium, zinc and manganese. Uranium output is worlds largest.
key_industry_3_desc: Astana International Financial Centre is a common law jurisdiction hub targeting Central Asian financial services.
key_industry_4_desc: Kazakhstan is a top global wheat and grain exporter. Arable land of 24M hectares with significant agri investment potential.
talent_overview: Kazakhstan has a highly educated workforce with Soviet era engineering and technical traditions. Kazakh and Russian are business languages.
talent_localisation_rule: Local content requirements apply in oil and gas sector. Targets for Kazakh national employment in foreign firms are increasing.
talent_foreign_worker_rule: Work permit required from Ministry of Labour. Quota based. Annual permit renewal required. Process takes 4 to 8 weeks.
talent_key_consideration: Russian language proficiency is important for management roles outside Astana and Almaty international business communities.
sector_priority_1_why: Major field expansions at Tengiz and Kashagan creating sustained demand for oilfield services and technology firms.
sector_priority_2_why: Astana IFC common law framework and 0% tax rate for qualifying firms creating attractive Central Asian financial hub opportunity.
sector_priority_3_why: Global critical mineral demand and Kazakhstan vast reserves creating significant mining technology and processing investment opportunity.
entry_playbook_overview: Kazakhstan offers multiple entry routes. AIFC is the most attractive for financial and professional services firms.
entry_step_1: Choose entry route — AIFC for financial services, standard LLP or JSC for other sectors, SEZ for manufacturing
entry_step_2: Register with Ministry of Justice — legal entity registration through e-government portal eGov.kz
entry_step_3: Register with State Revenue Committee — tax registration for CIT, VAT and social contributions
entry_step_4: Develop local content plan — mandatory for oil and gas sector. Broader sectors benefit from demonstrating Kazakh workforce commitment
current_conditions_summary: No direct exposure to the Iran conflict. Higher global oil prices (Brent above US$100 in late Sep 2026) and shipping disruption raise operating and logistics costs.

alerts.summary: Astana International Financial Centre announced expansion of permitted financial services activities and new tax incentives for qualifying firms establishing regional operations.

name: Kenya
main_industries: Tech · Finance · Agriculture · Tourism · Manufacturing
summary: East African hub with strong tech and innovation ecosystem
key_industry_1_desc: Nairobi is Africas Silicon Savannah. iHub, Konza Technopolis and 300+ tech startups make Kenya the continents tech leader.
key_industry_2_desc: M-Pesa transformed mobile money globally. Kenya has Africas highest financial inclusion rate at 83%.
key_industry_3_desc: Agriculture contributes 33% of GDP. Tea, coffee and horticulture are top exports. Agritech startups are transforming the sector.
key_industry_4_desc: Kenya is Africas premier safari destination generating $2B+ in annual tourism revenue with strong growth trajectory.
talent_overview: Kenya has East Africas strongest talent pool. English is an official language. Strong university sector producing tech and finance graduates.
talent_localisation_rule: Work permit quota requires firms to demonstrate no qualified Kenyan is available for the role being filled by an expatriate.
talent_foreign_worker_rule: Class G work permit required for expatriate employees. Dependent Pass available for family members.
talent_key_consideration: Kenya is the preferred East African HQ location for multinationals due to talent availability and English language proficiency.
sector_priority_1_why: Silicon Savannah ecosystem, young digital population and M-Pesa infrastructure make Kenya the top African tech investment destination.
sector_priority_2_why: Kenya already generates 90% renewable electricity. Green hydrogen and geothermal energy creating new investment opportunities.
sector_priority_3_why: AfCFTA regional trade and food security agenda creating strong demand for agritech and food processing investment.
entry_playbook_overview: Kenya is East Africas most straightforward market to enter. eCitizen portal streamlines registration significantly.
entry_step_1: Register via eCitizen portal — company registration takes 1 to 3 days online through the Registrar of Companies
entry_step_2: Register with KRA — Kenya Revenue Authority PIN registration for tax purposes is mandatory before operations begin
entry_step_3: Obtain sector licences — Capital Markets Authority for finance, Communications Authority for tech, relevant bodies for others
entry_step_4: Register with NSSF and NHIF — mandatory social security and health insurance registration for all employees

alerts.summary: Kenya Finance Act 2026 introduced digital services tax amendments and new VAT provisions for financial services. Effective July 2026.

name: Kuwait
main_industries: Oil & Gas · Finance · Real Estate · Retail
summary: Oil-rich economy with growing private sector diversification
key_industry_1_desc: Kuwait holds 6% of global oil reserves. KPC manages upstream and downstream operations with significant expansion plans.
key_industry_2_desc: Kuwait is home to one of the worlds largest sovereign wealth funds at $800B+ managed by Kuwait Investment Authority.
key_industry_3_desc: Kuwait Vision 2035 New Kuwait plan driving infrastructure investment in transport, housing and public facilities.
key_industry_4_desc: Government investing heavily in private healthcare capacity. Medical city projects creating significant PPP opportunities.
talent_overview: Kuwait workforce is 80% expatriate. Arabic is the official language but English widely used in business.
talent_localisation_rule: Kuwaitisation quotas apply across private sector. Financial sector requires 60% Kuwaiti nationals in senior roles.
talent_foreign_worker_rule: Work permit and residency visa required. Employer sponsored. Process can take 6 to 12 weeks.
talent_key_consideration: Public sector is heavily preferred by Kuwaiti nationals making private sector Kuwaitisation challenging in practice.
sector_priority_1_why: KPC expansion programme creating significant demand for oilfield services, technology and engineering firms.
sector_priority_2_why: Government PPP programme opening significant opportunities for private healthcare operators and medical technology firms.
sector_priority_3_why: New Kuwait 2035 plan committing billions to transport, housing and utilities infrastructure development.
entry_playbook_overview: Kuwait requires foreign firms to have a local Kuwaiti agent or partner for most commercial activities outside free zones.
entry_step_1: Identify a local Kuwaiti agent or partner — required for most government and commercial tender participation
entry_step_2: Register with Ministry of Commerce — obtain commercial licence through MOOCI single window system
entry_step_3: Register with Kuwait Tax Authority — corporate tax applies to foreign company shares of profits
entry_step_4: Register for Kuwait social insurance — required for all employees including expatriates in certain categories
geopolitical_alert: Among the most heavily targeted Gulf states; critical-infrastructure damage reported. Exports dependent on Hormuz.
current_conditions_summary: The Strait of Hormuz has been effectively closed to commercial shipping since 28 Feb 2026 (single-digit daily transits vs ~85 pre-crisis); the US naval blockade of Iran was reinstated in mid-July after the interim ceasefire collapsed. US–Iran talks are under way — on 23 Sep Iran tabled a road map including a 60-day regionwide ceasefire and phased reopening, not yet agreed. Kuwait was among the most heavily targeted states, including damage to utilities infrastructure and Kuwait International Airport.
current_conditions_factors: Infrastructure damage · Hormuz-dependent exports · Talks under way
current_conditions_outlook: Defer non-essential market entry until a durable ceasefire and Hormuz reopening.

name: Malaysia
main_industries: Semiconductors · Palm Oil · Finance · Tourism · Manufacturing
summary: Stable upper middle income economy with strong manufacturing base
key_industry_1_desc: Malaysia is the worlds 7th largest exporter of semiconductors. Penang is the Silicon Valley of the East hosting Intel, AMD and Infineon.
key_industry_2_desc: Malaysia is worlds 2nd largest palm oil producer. Downstream oleochemical processing is a growing value add sector.
key_industry_3_desc: Malaysia is the worlds largest Islamic finance market with $500B+ in assets. Bursa Malaysia is SEAs 3rd largest exchange.
key_industry_4_desc: Malaysia Digital Economy Blueprint targeting $22B in digital investment by 2025. Data centre investment is surging.
talent_overview: Malaysia has a multilingual professional workforce with strong English proficiency. Talent pool of 15M with good engineering and finance graduates.
talent_localisation_rule: Bumiputera equity participation requirements apply in certain sectors. Employment equity targets apply in government linked companies.
talent_foreign_worker_rule: Employment Pass for professionals earning MYR 5,000+. Approved by Immigration Department. Process takes 3 to 6 weeks.
talent_key_consideration: Malaysia offers the best combination of English proficiency, technical skills and cost competitiveness in Southeast Asia.
sector_priority_1_why: NIMP 2030 offering significant incentives for semiconductor and advanced manufacturing investment building on Penang cluster strength.
sector_priority_2_why: Hyperscaler investment in Malaysian data centres surging due to competitive power costs, political stability and connectivity.
sector_priority_3_why: Malaysia is the global centre of Islamic finance creating unique opportunity for Shariah compliant financial products and services.
entry_playbook_overview: Malaysia has a straightforward market entry process. SSM registration is fast. Sector specific incentives require MIDA engagement.
entry_step_1: Register with SSM — Companies Commission of Malaysia online registration takes 1 to 2 days
entry_step_2: Engage MIDA — Malaysian Investment Development Authority for manufacturing and technology investment incentives
entry_step_3: Register with LHDN and JKDM — Inland Revenue Board for corporate tax and Royal Customs for SST registration
entry_step_4: Apply for expatriate posts — MIDA or relevant ministry approval required before applying for Employment Passes

name: Nigeria
main_industries: Oil & Gas · Fintech · Agriculture · Telecoms · Entertainment
summary: Africas largest economy with high growth and high complexity
key_industry_1_desc: Nigeria is Africas fintech capital. Lagos hosts Flutterwave, Paystack and 200+ fintechs serving the continents largest unbanked population.
key_industry_2_desc: Nigeria is Africas largest oil producer. Dangote Refinery now operational transforming domestic refining capacity.
key_industry_3_desc: MTN, Airtel and Glo serve 200M+ subscribers. Data demand is surging driving infrastructure investment.
key_industry_4_desc: Nigeria is Africas largest agricultural economy. Government prioritising food processing to reduce imports.
talent_overview: Nigeria has Africas largest talent pool with 250M population and strong English language proficiency. Tech talent particularly strong.
talent_localisation_rule: Nigerian Content Act requires minimum local content in oil and gas sector. Other sectors have general preference requirements.
talent_foreign_worker_rule: Combined Expatriate Residence Permit and Alien Card required. Quota based on company capitalisation.
talent_key_consideration: Nigeria produces world class technology talent. Many diaspora professionals are returning creating a strong senior talent pipeline.
sector_priority_1_why: CBN regulatory reforms and 60M+ unbanked adults make Nigeria the most compelling fintech opportunity in Africa.

summary: Regional hub with 100% foreign ownership in free zones
key_industry_1_desc: DIFC is the regions premier financial hub hosting 5,000+ firms including global banks, asset managers and insurers.
key_industry_2_desc: Dubai welcomed 17M+ international visitors in 2023. Luxury, MICE and medical tourism are priority growth areas.
key_industry_3_desc: Jebel Ali is the worlds 9th largest port. UAE sits at the crossroads of Asia, Africa and Europe trade routes.
key_industry_4_desc: UAE targets 44% clean energy by 2050. Masdar City and DEWA projects are driving massive investment.
talent_overview: UAE workforce is 89% expatriate. English is the business language. Talent pool is large, diverse and internationally mobile.
talent_localisation_rule: Emiratisation applies to private sector firms with 50+ employees. Targets increase annually across skilled roles.
talent_foreign_worker_rule: Employment visa required. Sponsored by employer. Process typically takes 2 to 4 weeks.
talent_key_consideration: Competition for senior talent is intense. Compensation packages typically include housing, schooling and flights.
sector_priority_1_why: DIFC and ADGM offer world class regulatory frameworks with 0% tax and 100% foreign ownership for financial firms.
sector_priority_2_why: UAE Net Zero 2050 strategy is driving billions in solar, hydrogen and clean tech investment opportunities.
sector_priority_3_why: Ageing expat population and medical tourism ambition driving strong demand for healthcare infrastructure and services.
entry_playbook_overview: UAE offers two primary entry routes — mainland and free zone — each with distinct ownership, tax and operational implications.
entry_step_1: Choose your structure — Free zone for 100% ownership and tax benefits, or Mainland for broader market access
entry_step_2: Select your jurisdiction — Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Sharjah each offer different free zones suited to different sectors
entry_step_3: Obtain your trade licence — Commercial, professional or industrial licence depending on activity
entry_step_4: Open corporate bank account — Allow 4 to 8 weeks. Requires full KYC documentation and business plan
geopolitical_alert: Hormuz effectively closed since 28 Feb 2026; Jebel Ali and re-export trade heavily disrupted. US–Iran talks under way (Iran proposed a 60-day ceasefire on 23 Sep).
current_conditions_summary: The Strait of Hormuz has been effectively closed to commercial shipping since 28 Feb 2026 (single-digit daily transits vs ~85 pre-crisis); the US naval blockade of Iran was reinstated in mid-July after the interim ceasefire collapsed. US–Iran talks are under way — on 23 Sep Iran tabled a road map including a 60-day regionwide ceasefire and phased reopening, not yet agreed. The UAE was among the most frequently targeted states in earlier strike waves; Jebel Ali throughput and re-export flows remain heavily disrupted.
current_conditions_factors: Hormuz closure · Elevated strike exposure · Logistics rerouting · Talks under way
current_conditions_outlook: Structural fundamentals remain strong; near-term conditions depend on the outcome of US–Iran talks. Re-test timing and business-continuity plans before committing capital.

alerts.summary: UAE Ministry of Finance issued updated guidance on qualifying free zone entity rules.

name: Vietnam
main_industries: Manufacturing · Electronics · Agriculture · Tourism · Technology
summary: Fastest growing manufacturing hub replacing China supply chains
key_industry_1_desc: Vietnam is the worlds 2nd largest exporter of electronics after China. Samsung, Intel and LG have major manufacturing operations.
key_industry_2_desc: Vietnam has 500,000+ software engineers. Ho Chi Minh City is emerging as a major technology outsourcing hub.
key_industry_3_desc: Vietnam is worlds top exporter of cashews, pepper and tra fish. Seafood exports exceed $9B annually.
key_industry_4_desc: Vietnam installed 16GW of solar in 2020 to 2021 alone. Offshore wind pipeline is one of Asias largest.
talent_overview: Vietnam has a young workforce of 56M with strong engineering and technical education. Vietnamese is the business language with English growing in multinationals.
talent_localisation_rule: Foreign workers cannot exceed 20% of total workforce except in specific circumstances approved by provincial authorities.
talent_foreign_worker_rule: Work permit required from Ministry of Labour. Labour demand report required before applying. Process takes 4 to 6 weeks.
talent_key_consideration: Vietnam offers Asia Pacifics best combination of cost, technical skill and political stability for manufacturing investment.
sector_priority_1_why: China plus one strategy making Vietnam the top destination for electronics and high tech manufacturing relocation from China.
sector_priority_2_why: Large pool of cost competitive software engineers and government IT sector incentives driving strong technology investment.
sector_priority_3_why: Vietnam has Asias best offshore wind resources and a government target of 6GW by 2030 creating major project pipeline.
entry_playbook_overview: Vietnam requires an Investment Registration Certificate for foreign investors. Process managed through provincial Department of Planning and Investment.
entry_step_1: Obtain Investment Registration Certificate — apply to Department of Planning and Investment in chosen province
entry_step_2: Obtain Enterprise Registration Certificate — business registration following IRC approval typically takes 3 to 5 days
entry_step_3: Register with tax authority — obtain tax code and register for VAT and corporate income tax
entry_step_4: Open bank account and remit charter capital — minimum charter capital must be remitted within 90 days of IRC
current_conditions_summary: No direct exposure to the Iran conflict. Higher global oil prices (Brent above US$100 in late Sep 2026) and shipping disruption raise operating and logistics costs.
current_conditions_factors: Normal business environment · Standard regulatory monitoring · No elevated conflict exposure
current_conditions_outlook: Current conditions broadly consistent with structural fundamentals. Standard market entry timing considerations apply.

alerts.title: Corporate Tax Incentives Revised
alerts.summary: Vietnam revised preferential corporate tax rates for high tech and innovation sector investments.

alerts.title: Global Minimum Tax Implementation
alerts.summary: Vietnam formally enacted 15% global minimum tax for large multinational enterprises effective January 2026 in line with OECD Pillar Two framework.
